source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Leviticus 26–27. The exact original XML records include all three annotations at 26:7, 26:8 and 26:28; no numbering shift occurs in this batch.

key_decisions.decision: Unfolds the compressed persons-and-valuation clause without depicting the person as an ordinary animal offering; special vow is a noted lexical choice.
Keeps sex, both stated age endpoints, exact amount, silver and sanctuary standard without assigning a moral worth to the valuation.
Distinguishes the person vowed from the person paying where the pronoun is compressed; preserves the priest’s assessment based on means, with referent uncertainty noted.
Retains both forbidden directions of exchange and the consequence for both animals, even where the substitute seems better.
Makes seed capacity the field-assessment basis; retains barley, homer and fifty shekels without importing modern land area or crop yield.
Uses a passive for the disputed seller while retaining nonredemption, sale and permanent loss of redemption; note preserves alternative subjects and logical connection.
Keeps Jubilee release distinct from return to the original family and introduces herem’s irrevocable category with the priest as recipient.
Keeps that-day payment as written rather than silently adding Jubilee before day; distinguishes payment timing from the valuation endpoint.
Keeps the already-due restriction and renders seh with sheep and goats instead of excluding goats from the category.
Retains ransom and redeem verbs, extra fifth only for redemption, and sale at assessed value; note leaves the unclean animal’s connection to firstborn open.
Preserves all three categories including people, both prohibitions and most-holy status; herem is distinguished from an ordinary redeemable vow.
Preserves the explicit human death penalty and nonransomability without inventing a limitation to war prisoners or implying every ordinary vow is lethal.
Retains the actual tenth-animal procedure and rod image, with flock including sheep and goats rather than sheep alone.
Keeps the prohibition of selecting by quality and exchanging, and applies holy/nonredeemable status to both animals.
